channel.title: interviews on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in interviews on Loud Legends

item.title: Legendary LED ZEPPELIN Vocalist ROBERT PLANT Reveals Why He Decided To Skip OZZY OSBOURNE's Farewell Concert
item.description: Robert Plant says he turned down Tony Iommi’s invitation to Ozzy Osbourne’s farewell because the stadium-scale metal world isn’t where his head is anymore. He didn’t slam it.

item.title: Paul Stanley Reveals KISS’s Biggest Song of All Time: 'Massive Hit, Yet Unlike Anything We’d Done Before'
item.description: Paul Stanley isn’t hedging. He called “I Was Made for Lovin’ You” the biggest KISS song of all time, pointing to 1.3 billion Spotify streams and roughly 850,000 daily plays as of late August.

item.title: The Only Punk Band Ozzy Osbourne Ever Liked (Even Though He Couldn't Stand the Singer)
item.description: By the late 1970s, punk rock was gaining momentum. Ozzy Osbourne, however, was already deep into his career, with Black Sabbath having helped lay the foundation for what would become heavy metal.

item.title: Nicko McBrain Fires Back at IRON MAIDEN’s New Drummer, Declares ‘He’s Not Me’ and Says Band Can’t Replace 42 Years of History
item.description: Former Iron Maiden drummer Nicko McBrain is enjoying life after retirement, but he’s still got a few things to say, especially about the band he spent over four decades performing with.

item.title: Ozzy Osbourne Once Said He Wanted a Beatles Song Played at His Funeral
item.description: English singer and songwriter Ozzy Osbourne, best known as the original frontman of Black Sabbath and for his solo career under his own name, died on Tuesday, July 22, at the age of 76.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says DAVE MUSTAINE Wanted to Re-Record METALLICA Demo
item.description: In a recent episode of The David Ellefson Show, former Megadeth bassist David Ellefson shared some revealing details about his final years with the band, focusing on what he described as a toxic environment and an unexpected proposal from Dave Mustaine.

item.title: How OZZY OSBOURNE Would Like to Be Remembered, According to His Own Words
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne, the voice behind Black Sabbath and a pillar of heavy metal history, died on Tuesday, July 22, at age 76. Fans around the world are mourning the loss of the man who helped define the genre with a mix of raw energy, chaos, and oddly enough, heartfelt honesty.

item.title: TONY IOMMI Says OZZY OSBOURNE Pushed Through Final Show: 'He Didn't Look Well'
item.description: In his first public comments since Ozzy Osbourne’s death, Tony Iommi told ITV News the loss caught him off guard. Even though Ozzy’s health had clearly declined in recent months, Iommi didn’t expect things to end so soon (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: Jack White of The White Stripes Slams Trump Over Redskins Name Flip-Flop
item.description: Jack White, known for his work with The White Stripes and a long solo career, is calling out former President Donald Trump over two contradictory posts about the Washington NFL team’s name.

item.title: ANDI DERIS Says He Abandoned IRON MAIDEN After Paul Di’Anno Was Replaced by Bruce Dickinson
item.description: Andi Deris, longtime vocalist of Helloween, recently opened up about a personal turning point as a heavy metal fan. In a chat with the Scars and Guitars podcast, Deris explained how he reacted when Bruce Dickinson joined Iron Maiden in the early 1980s, replacing original frontman Paul Di’Anno.

item.title: Linkin Park's MIKE SHINODA Says Fan Backlash to EMILY ARMSTRONG Was About Gender: 'She Wasn't a Guy'
item.description: Linkin Park’s return to the stage after a seven-year break has been met with applause, confusion, and loud opinions online. The band has a new album, a global tour, and a different voice at the front of the stage: Emily Armstrong, formerly of Dead Sara.

item.title: MEGADETH’s DAVE MUSTAINE Reached Out to Join OZZY OSBOURNE and BLACK SABBATH’s 'Back To The Beginning' Final Show, But 'Nothing Came of It', Says LOMENZO
item.description: Megadeth bassist James LoMenzo says the band was not invited to perform at “Back To The Beginning”, the high-profile charity concert that celebrated Black Sabbath’s final show. The event took place in Birmingham, UK on July 5.

item.title: The Metallica Megahit Classic That 'SUCKS', According To JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: In a not-so-recent behind-the-scenes video, Metallica fans got an unexpected moment: James Hetfield, frontman of one of the most famous metal bands on the planet, didn’t hold back when asked about one of the group’s earliest hits.

item.title: When DAVE MUSTAINE Was Surprised By METALLICA's JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Didn't Think He Knew How to Play'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t always see James Hetfield as a guitarist. In fact, the first time he saw Hetfield pick up a guitar, he was genuinely surprised. The Megadeth frontman shared this moment in a 2023 interview with Metal Hammer, reflecting on the early days of Metallica, long before either band became a household name in heavy metal.

item.title: The Guitarist ANGUS YOUNG Once Blamed For Setting ROCK MUSIC Back Two Decades: 'Jeez, It Sounds So Dated'
item.description: Angus Young , the longtime AC/DC guitarist, is known for his stripped-down style, blistering riffs, and no-nonsense views on what makes a good guitar player. Over the years, he’s made his opinion clear about effects pedals, tremolo bars, and overly polished guitar work.

item.title: NO IRON MAIDEN; The Two Songs Bruce Dickinson Believes Explain Everything You Need To Know About Rock MUSIC
item.description: Iron Maiden frontman Bruce Dickinson has built a reputation as one of heavy metal’s most iconic voices. But when it comes to understanding rock and roll at its core, Dickinson doesn’t reach for one of his own band’s classic tracks.

item.title: DARON MALAKIAN Breaks Silence on Why SYSTEM OF A DOWN Won't Release New Album: 'Where Do You Pick Up From?'
item.description: Daron Malakian, guitarist and one of the founding members of System of a Down, recently shared his thoughts on why the band probably will not release a new studio album anytime soon.

item.title: 'It Scared The @#$% Out Of Me': JAMES HETFIELD Reveals The Real Story Behind METALLICA’s Darkest Song
item.description: Metallica’s frontman James Hetfield has never shied away from heavy topics. Over the decades, he’s written lyrics about death, addiction, war, and emotional isolation. But there’s one track in particular that stands out to him as the band’s darkest.

item.title: Brent Smith Says ‘The Audience Is the Boss’ as Shinedown Releases New Single ‘Killing Fields’; Watch
item.description: Shinedown has released a new single called Killing Fields (listen below). The track is now available on all major streaming platforms. It was released through Atlantic Records.

item.title: Killswitch Engage's JESSE LEACH Reflects On Tour Life: 'We Owe It To The Fans, Dude'
item.description: Killswitch Engage singer Jesse Leach opened up about the pressures of touring and how he protects his voice on the road. In a recent interview with American Musical Supply, Leach explained his routine for staying healthy and keeping his vocals in shape while traveling.

item.title: MORGAN LANDER Explains Why KITTIE No Longer Fits The 'Nu Metal' Label: 'We’re Not Trying To Recapture The Past'
item.description: Kittie frontwoman Morgan Lander says the band has outgrown the nu metal tag. In a new interview with Metalshop TV, the guitarist and vocalist said that calling Kittie a nu metal band no longer fits what they sound like.

item.title: Former SLIPKNOT Drummer JAY WEINBERG Says Upcoming Solo Album Reflects Years of Quiet Work and Creative Freedom: 'I'm Playing Everything on It'
item.description: Former Slipknot drummer Jay Weinberg is preparing to release his first solo album, a project he has quietly developed over the past decade. Speaking on the Podioslave Podcast, Weinberg described the work as deeply personal, creatively ambitious, and long overdue.

item.title: Mötley Crüe bassist NIKKI SIXX Explains DOLLY PARTON Collab: 'She Was a Hard Yes'
item.description: Mötley Crüe and Dolly Parton have released a new version of Home Sweet Home to mark the song’s 40th anniversary. The track debuted at No. 1 on the Mediabase Classic Rock Songs chart in June.

item.title: The One Musician JAMES HETFIELD Believed Was Just 'Too Good' For METALLICA: 'No Way He’s Going To Join Us'
item.description: When Robert Trujillo joined Metallica in 2003, the band wasn’t just looking for a good bassist. They needed someone who could match their work ethic, play with power, and bring stability after years of lineup changes and creative friction.

item.title: KELLY OSBOURNE Doesn’t Hold Back After Bizarre VIRAL AI Video Claims OZZY and SHARON Made a Private End-of-Life Decision
item.description: Kelly Osbourne is setting the record straight about her parents, Ozzy and Sharon Osbourne. The TV personality and daughter of the legendary rocker addressed growing rumors on social media suggesting that her parents had entered a so-called “suicide pact” to end their lives together if their health deteriorated.

item.title: NIKKI SIXX Reveals Why MÖTLEY CRÜE Were Missing From OZZY OSBOURNE’s Farewell Show
item.description: Fans of Mötley Crüe noticed something missing during Ozzy Osbourne’s massive Back to the Beginning farewell concert in Birmingham: the Crüe themselves. The event, held on July 5, was billed as a once-in-a-lifetime celebration.

item.title: The Controversial Reason METALLICA Members Didn’t Like JASON NEWSTED, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: In a revealing interview from 2018, Metallica frontman James Hetfield opened up about a difficult chapter in the band’s history: their treatment of bassist Jason Newsted, who joined the group following the death of Cliff Burton in 1986.

item.title: Is This How It Ends? AARON STAINTHORPE Unsure If He’s Still the Vocalist of MY DYING BRIDE
item.description: Aaron Stainthorpe isn’t entirely sure whether he’s still the lead singer of My Dying Bride. The British doom metal band recently returned to the stage with Mikko Kotamäki, from Swallow the Sun, handling vocals.

item.title: HALESTORM Drops New Song 'RAIN YOUR BLOOD ON ME' From Upcoming Album 'EVEREST'
item.description: Halestorm has released a new single titled “Rain Your Blood On Me,” giving fans another preview of the band’s next studio album, Everest, due out August 8 through Atlantic Records (listen below).

item.title: Ghost's TOBIAS FORGE Says He Wanted to Perform a Different Song at BLACK SABBATH’s Farewell Show: 'No! Already Taken'
item.description: Tobias Forge, the voice behind Ghost, recently shared that his first pick for Black Sabbath’s farewell show didn’t make the cut. The singer was one of many artists invited to perform at Back to the Beginning, a massive farewell event for Black Sabbath and Ozzy Osbourne.

item.title: DEFTONES Return With New Album PRIVATE MUSIC And First Single 'MY MIND IS A MOUNTAIN'; VIDEO
item.description: Deftones are officially back. The California alt-metal band has announced their new album, private music, and dropped its lead single, “my mind is a mountain,” along with a brand-new music video (watch below).

item.title: TONY IOMMI Reveals the BLACK SABBATH Songs That Were Rehearsed but Cut From the Final 'BACK TO THE BEGINNING' Setlist
item.description: Tony Iommi says Black Sabbath had a longer setlist in mind for their recent reunion show, but time and circumstances forced them to cut it short. During a new interview with Eddie Trunk on SiriusXM’s Trunk Nation (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Former PEARL JAM Drummer DAVE ABBRUZZESE Breaks Silence on Rumored Comeback After MATT CAMERON Exit
item.description: Matt Cameron recently stepped away from his role as drummer for Pearl Jam, ending a nearly 30-year run. He didn’t explain why, and the band hasn’t named a replacement, leaving fans and the music press to fill in the blanks.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Receives 'Unbelievable' Emotional Gift From YUNGBLUD Before Final BLACK SABBATH Performance in Birmingham; VIDEO
item.description: As Ozzy Osbourne prepared to take the stage one last time with Black Sabbath, another artist was waiting backstage with something a bit unexpected. Yungblud, the genre-bending musician from Doncaster, brought more than just his performance to Villa Park in Birmingham.

item.title: JOHN BUSH Explains Why He Rejected METALLICA: 'They Were Nobodies Back Then'
item.description: John Bush, best known for fronting Armored Saint and later Anthrax, recently spoke in depth about the time he was offered a spot as Metallica’s lead singer.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Teased A Post-Show Reveal About The Band She Banned From OZZY's Farewell, But We Might Already Know Who It Is
item.description: For a concert billed as Back to the Beginning, meant to close the book on the legacy of Black Sabbath and mark Ozzy Osbourne’s final bow, one detail stood out more for what was missing than what was onstage.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Confirms OZZY's Touring Days Are Over: 'He's Done. We're Going Home And Shutting The Door'
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne’s long career on stage has officially come to a close. His final live performance took place on Saturday, July 5, during Back to the Beginning, a special concert event in Birmingham, the hometown of Black Sabbath.

item.title: Godsmack's SULLY ERNA Pays Tribute to OZZY OSBOURNE: 'Another Childhood Hero Has Taken His Final Bow'
item.description: Godsmack singer Sully Erna has shared a heartfelt message honoring Ozzy Osbourne, following the rock icon’s final show in Birmingham, England. The “Back to the Beginning” concert on July 5 marked the end of an era, as Ozzy performed one last time for over 40,000 fans at Villa Park.

item.title: SLIPKNOT Launches Cryptic Website With Countdown, Hints At 25th Anniversary Album Reissue
item.description: Slipknot is building anticipation with a cryptic online campaign that points toward a special 25th anniversary edition of their self-titled 1999 debut album. The band has launched a mysterious new website, 742617000027.

item.title: The Songs METALLICA Chose to Say 'Thank You' to BLACK SABBATH in Front of 40,000+ Fans
item.description: Metallica showed up loud, fast, and full of gratitude at Black Sabbath’s final concert, delivering a powerful six-song set that included two unexpected tributes to the band that helped create heavy metal.

item.title: Spinal Tap Director ROB REINER Calls BLACK SABBATH 'Dumb' Over Stonehenge Accusation: 'It’s Ridiculous'
item.description: The director behind This Is Spinal Tap is calling out Black Sabbath for something that happened over 40 years ago, and he’s not pulling any punches. In a recent interview with Screen Rant, filmmaker Rob Reiner revisited a long-standing misunderstanding between the legendary heavy metal band and the makers of the cult comedy film.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Says When She'll Reveal Which Band Was Cut From BLACK SABBATH's Final Show: 'People Will Be Shocked'
item.description: As Black Sabbath prepares to take the stage for the last time at Villa Park, the band’s farewell concert is already generating headlines. This time, it’s not the music or the massive lineup drawing attention.

item.title: SOAD's SHAVO ODADJIAN Says Phone Bans At Shows 'Take Something Away' From Fans: 'I Catch Myself Filming Sometimes Too'
item.description: Shavo Odadjian, bassist of System of a Down, doesn’t believe in taking away your phone at a concert. In a recent Q&A with readers of Metal Hammer, Odadjian shared his thoughts on phone-free shows, a practice growing in popularity among artists looking to keep fans more engaged during live performances.

item.title: TONY IOMMI Reveals How Many Songs OZZY OSBOURNE Will Sing at BLACK SABBATH's Final Concert: 'He Can’t Do the Whole Show'
item.description: Black Sabbath is getting ready to take the stage one last time. The band’s final performance, set for Saturday, July 5, will take place in their hometown of Birmingham, England.

item.title: SLIPKNOT’s COREY TAYLOR Explains Why He Keeps Returning to a 1970 BLACK SABBATH Track That Still Terrifies Him
item.description: Slipknot frontman Corey Taylor still remembers the chill he got the first time he heard Black Sabbath, the song, not just the band. In a recent interview with the BBC, Taylor shared how deeply the track affected him.

item.title: The One Band CHRIS CORNELL Believed Was America’s Answer To LED ZEPPELIN
item.description: Long before grunge made Seattle famous, Chris Cornell had already picked his local musical heroes. Among British rock influences, there was one American band he saw as a standout.

item.title: KALEN CHASE Explains Why VIMIC Won’t Continue Without JOEY JORDISON: 'There Are No Plans for Future Stuff'
item.description: VIMIC, the metal project formed by late Slipknot drummer Joey Jordison, is set to take the stage one last time. On October 3, the band will reunite for a tribute concert in Los Angeles.

item.title: The Legendary Musician Who Made JAMES HETFIELD Rethink His Entire Creative Process
item.description: Even after more than four decades with Metallica, James Hetfield is still learning. The frontman has spoken about what keeps him motivated creatively, crediting an unexpected influence, Elton John, with challenging the way he approaches songwriting and performance.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Confirms Live Retirement: 'It’s A Goodbye As Far As My Live Performances Go'
item.description: In a new interview promoting this weekend’s Back to the Beginning event, the legendary Black Sabbath frontman confirmed that his upcoming concert at Villa Park in Birmingham, England, will be his final time performing live.

item.title: The Disgusting Reason Metallica's JAMES HETFIELD Hates LOAD and RELOAD Album Covers
item.description: Metallica’s mid-’90s albums, Load and Reload, are remembered for more than just a shift in musical style. Their cover art caused a stir too, especially with frontman James Hetfield.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Hated The Direction Metallica Took In The ‘90s: 'So Stupid'
item.description: In a 2001 interview with Playboy, Metallica frontman James Hetfield reflected on the band’s major style shift during the Load era. For Hetfield, that period, complete with designer clothes, makeup, and fashionable haircuts, wasn’t exactly a high point.

item.title: How One EMBARRASSING Night at 'Whiskey A Go Go' Forced LINKIN PARK to Find CHESTER BENNINGTON
item.description: Linkin Park rose to become one of the most influential rock bands of the 21st century. Known for blending heavy guitar riffs, hip-hop beats, and electronic layers, the group built a sound that was both accessible and intense.

item.title: KITTIE’s Comeback Wasn’t Planned, Says MERCEDES LANDER: 'We Just Wanted To Play A Couple Shows'
item.description: Canadian metal band KITTIE is back with a new album, but the comeback wasn’t part of a grand plan. In a recent interview with Loud TV (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), drummer Mercedes Lander explained how the return came together almost by accident.

item.title: Oasis' NOEL GALLAGHER Criticizes Artists at Glastonbury Festival: 'Play Your F*ing Tunes and Get Off'
item.description: Noel Gallagher has spoken out against Glastonbury, calling the music festival “woke” and full of “virtue-signaling.” The Oasis guitarist made the comments in a recent interview on the Matt Morgan podcast, just before this year’s festival began (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: SEPULTURA’s Derrick Green Says His Parents Supported His Music From the Start: 'They Were Very Open-Minded'
item.description: Derrick Green, longtime frontman of the Brazilian metal band SEPULTURA, recently opened up about how his parents reacted when he first started screaming into a microphone. In a new interview with Finland’s Chaoszine (watch below), Green said his parents were “very open-minded” about his decision to become a musician, even when his early performances were loud and intense.

item.title: The Singer METALLICA Wanted Before JAMES HETFIELD, But He Said No
item.description: James Hetfield is the face and voice of Metallica, one of the biggest heavy metal bands in the world. His gritty voice, aggressive rhythm guitar playing, and songwriting skills have helped define the band’s sound since the early 1980s.

item.title: The Song That Annoyed JAMES HETFIELD, but METALLICA Covered Anyway: 'It Drove Me Nuts'
item.description: James Hetfield has built a career on intensity and control, but even he has moments where personal taste takes a back seat. One of those moments came in the late 1990s, when Metallica recorded “Turn the Page” for their 1998 cover album Garage Inc.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT’s WES BORLAND’s Controversial Take on Heavy Metal: 'Boring As F*ck'
item.description: Wes Borland, guitarist for Limp Bizkit, has never exactly fit the mold of a typical nü-metal poster boy. Known for his elaborate stage costumes and artistic detours, Borland has always appeared slightly out of place next to Fred Durst’s red Yankees cap and the band’s frat-rap aggression.

item.title: The Song JAMES HETFIELD Considers the Greatest of All, and Countless Bands Have Tried to Recreate
item.description: James Hetfield has always worn his influences on his sleeve. In a recent episode of The Metallica Report (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), the Metallica frontman named Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” as the greatest song of all time.

item.title: FAITH NO MORE’s Mike Bordin Says OZZY OSBOURNE Saved His Life: 'You’re the reason I’m here'
item.description: When Faith No More released The Real Thing in June 1989, it marked more than just their third studio album. It was the first with vocalist Mike Patton and quickly became a defining moment for the band.

item.title: Why One of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Old Rivals Agreed to Play at BLACK SABBATH’s Farewell Show
item.description: Jake E. Lee hasn’t spoken to Ozzy Osbourne in decades. The two didn’t exactly part ways on good terms, and there’s been little reason for contact since Lee was fired back in the ’80s.

item.title: What ANGUS YOUNG Thinks About Fans Who Rejected AXL ROSE As AC/DC’s Singer
item.description: In an interview with Rolling Stone in 2021, guitarist Angus Young opened up about a moment that split fans of AC/DC, when Axl Rose stepped in as lead singer during their 2016 tour.

item.title: The Vulnerable METALLICA Song That Set The Band On A New Path, According To JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: For a band known for thrash, fire, and a habit of rattling stadium foundations, Metallica’s transformation didn’t happen with a single riff or overnight revelation. It was a slow burn.

item.title: KIRK HAMMETT Opens Up About Comparing Himself To New Guitarists: 'Where Did I Go Wrong? I Should Be Much Better'
item.description: Kirk Hammett might have four decades with Metallica under his belt, but if you ask him, he’s not exactly resting on his reputation. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, the longtime guitarist was asked to reflect on how he sees himself as a player.

item.title: GENE HOGLAN Says METALLICA’s 'One' Echoes DARK ANGEL: 'That Beat Came From Us'
item.description: In a recent interview, Gene Hoglan, drummer for the thrash metal band Dark Angel, shared his thoughts on a long-standing theory among metal fans, that Metallica’s 1988 track “One” was inspired by Dark Angel’s 1986 song “Darkness Descends.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Breaks Down the Goal of New METALLICA Doc: 'Turn The Spotlight Away From Us And Celebrate The Fans'
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich wants people to know the band isn’t the main focus of their new documentary. The real stars, he says, are the fans. Speaking on the red carpet at the Tribeca Festival premiere of Metallica Saved My Life, Ulrich explained why the film shifts attention away from the band and onto the people who have supported them for more than four decades.

item.title: HALESTORM Releases New Music Video for 'DARKNESS ALWAYS WINS': 'Evil Prevails And The Good Depart First'
item.description: Halestorm has unveiled a new official video for “Darkness Always Wins,” the band’s first release of 2025 (watch it below). Directed by DJay Brawner and produced by Dave Cobb, the song builds slowly with a cinematic tone and sits firmly in the band’s hard rock catalog.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Says He Wants To Work With PAUL MCCARTNEY: 'I Would Be Honoured'
item.description: During a new episode of Ozzy Speaks on SiriusXM (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Ozzy Osbourne mentioned that he would like to collaborate with Paul McCartney. The rock icon discussed the idea while chatting with his co-host, Billy Morrison.

item.title: Dream Theater's MIKE PORTNOY Defends LARS ULRICH: 'He Takes a Beating, But He's Invaluable'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for Dream Theater, says Lars Ulrich deserves more credit. In a recent chat with El Estepario Siberiano (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Portnoy explained why he thinks the Metallica co-founder is often misunderstood.

item.title: The Two METALLICA Songs JAMES HETFIELD Finds 'Truly Difficult' To Perform Live: 'Really Messes With Me'
item.description: Metallica has been around for over 40 years, and their music is known for being fast, loud, and often complex. But for frontman James Hetfield, two songs from their 2008 album Death Magnetic still stand out as especially difficult to play live.

item.title: How METALLICA Fooled Audiences in the Early Days, According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'We Took All The Credit'
item.description: Metallica, one of the most recognized names in heavy metal, wasn’t always the arena-dominating force it is today. Back in 1981, when James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich first formed the band, they didn’t have a vault of original songs ready to go.

item.title: WOLFGANG VAN HALEN Explains Why He Backed Out of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final Concert: 'I Wouldn’t Be Able To Pull It Off'
item.description: Wolfgang Van Halen, son of late guitar legend Eddie Van Halen, was originally scheduled to appear at Ozzy Osbourne’s farewell concert, Back to the Beginning, on July 5 in Birmingham, U.

item.title: Why IRON MAIDEN Turned To Japan Before Chasing The American Dream, According to ROD SMALLWOOD
item.description: Iron Maiden’s first real step onto the global stage came in 1981, the same year the band dropped Killers and hit the road for their first world tour.

item.title: The Guitarist TOM MORELLO Fought To Bring Back For Black Sabbath’s Last Show: 'I Can’t Imagine This Happening Without You'
item.description: Tom Morello is playing a key role in organizing Black Sabbath’s last concert. And for him, one name was essential: Jake E. Lee, the guitarist who played with Ozzy Osbourne in the 1980s.

item.title: Ex-Mastodon BRENT HINDS Slams Former Bandmates In Exit Statement: 'A S**t Band With Horrible Humans'
item.description: Brent Hinds, the former guitarist and vocalist of Mastodon, didn’t exactly offer a warm farewell. In a blunt comment on Instagram, he referred to the group as a “s**t band with horrible humans.

item.title: The Band EDDIE VAN HALEN Believed Saved Rock ‘n’ Roll From Extinction: 'Rock Wouldn’t Exist Without Them'
item.description: Rock music has had plenty of supposed saviors. Every few decades, someone new gets the credit for dragging the genre back from the brink. Eddie Van Halen was one of those names, but according to him, his own rise might not have happened without a much earlier band shaking things up.

item.title: Metallica's KIRK HAMMETT Recalls Struggling With 'The Unforgiven': 'I Wasn't Prepared For It'
item.description: Metallica guitarist Kirk Hammett is known for writing some of the band’s most famous guitar parts, but not every one came easy. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, he opened up about the difficulties he faced while working on the solo for “The Unforgiven”, one of the standout tracks from the band’s 1991 self-titled release, often called “The Black Album.

item.title: The One Drummer PHIL COLLINS Admired But Called Out For Having A Massive Ego: 'The Size of a Hotel'
item.description: Phil Collins wasn’t just the voice that brought pop stardom to Genesis. He also helped redefine how drums were recorded in the 1980s, built a massive solo career, and even teamed up with unexpected names, like when he played with Led Zeppelin.

item.title: SCORPIONS/Ex-MOTÖRHEAD MIKKEY DEE Admits He Felt Lost Playing With KING DIAMOND: 'I Was A Lousy Drummer'
item.description: Mikkey Dee, born Micael Kiriakos Delaoglou in Gothenburg, Sweden, got his big break playing drums for King Diamond. But in a recent interview with Rock Kommander (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: The BLACK SABBATH Song That Blew Led Zeppelin's JOHN BONHAM’s Mind
item.description: Before joining Led Zeppelin and becoming a rock legend, John Bonham was already turning heads in the music scene of England’s Black Country. As a teenager, just 16 years old, he crossed paths with a fellow drummer: Bill Ward, who would later power Black Sabbath’s thunderous rhythm section.

item.title: MIKE PORTNOY Says LARS ULRICH Was a Major Influence: 'He Was More Than Just a Drummer'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for progressive metal band Dream Theater, recently shared that Lars Ulrich of Metallica had a big impact on his career, and not just behind the drum kit.

item.title: VENOM INC.'s TONY DOLAN Reacts To Public Accusations From MANTAS: 'They All Blame Me For Their Own Demise'
item.description: Tony Dolan is setting the record straight. The bassist and vocalist of VENOM INC. recently addressed his fallout with guitarist Jeff “Mantas” Dunn, who officially left the band in late 2023.

item.title: Watch FEMME FATALE's New Video for 'Living Like There's No Tomorrow'
item.description: Femme Fatale, the rock band led by Lorraine Lewis, has returned with a new song called “Living Like There’s No Tomorrow” (watch it below). The track is now available through Cleopatra Records, and its official music video, directed by Vicente Cordero, is out now.

item.title: JACOBY SHADDIX Talks New PAPA ROACH Single With TOBY MORSE: 'It Felt Urgent, Honest, In Your Face'
item.description: Papa Roach is back with a new single, and they’ve brought along a longtime friend. The California rock band just released “Braindead” (watch it below), a high-energy track featuring Toby Morse, the lead singer of punk band H2O.

item.title: JAKE E. LEE Asks Fans Not To Judge OZZY OSBOURNE’s Performance: 'He Deserves This Farewell'
item.description: Guitarist Jake E. Lee is urging fans to show compassion ahead of Back to the Beginning, the farewell concert for Ozzy Osbourne and the original Black Sabbath lineup.

item.title: FRANK BELLO Says His Grandmother's Final Show Was ANTHRAX At Yankee Stadium: 'She Loved It'
item.description: Anthrax bassist Frank Bello has shared a personal memory from one of the biggest shows of his career, the Big Four concert at Yankee Stadium in 2011.

item.title: The RUSH Album That Led to Fan Backlash, Internal Tension, and a Moment of Regret: 'It Wasn’t the Smartest Move'
item.description: Most bands with long careers eventually take a creative detour. Whether to keep things fresh or avoid burnout, they try something new. Sometimes it works. Sometimes it doesn’t.

item.title: When MAX CAVALERA Almost Reunited With SEPULTURA: 'We'll Cross Paths Again'
item.description: Max Cavalera is best known for helping create one of Brazil’s most influential metal bands: Sepultura. But in 1996, after years of success, he walked away from it all.

item.title: SEBASTIAN BACH Talks Dimebag Darrell’s Wild Hotel Incident: 'He Stabbed The Couch On Acid'
item.description: Sebastian Bach recently shared a wild story from his days on tour with Pantera. The former Skid Row frontman opened up in a new interview about a chaotic moment involving the late Dimebag Darrell, a knife, and a hotel lobby couch (via Sense Music Media) (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says DAVE MUSTAINE ‘Hated Playing Before SLAYER’ On 2010 Tour
item.description: Dave Mustaine wasn’t happy with his spot on the lineup during MEGADETH’s tours with SLAYER, according to former bandmate David Ellefson. In a recent episode of The David Ellefson Show podcast (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), the former MEGADETH bassist spoke about the 2010 Jägermeister Music Tour.

item.title: AARON STAINTHORPE Talks Leaving MY DYING BRIDE: 'I Feel 10 Years Younger'
item.description: Aaron Stainthorpe, known for fronting British metal band My Dying Bride for over three decades, says his new project has given him a fresh perspective, and a second wind.

item.title: The Problem With 'LOAD' and 'RELOAD', According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Hate That Part Of Us'
item.description: Metallica made a name for itself in the early days with fast, aggressive thrash metal. But things changed with the release of their self-titled album in 1991, known to most as the Black Album.

item.title: What Growing Up Was Like for DAVE MUSTAINE: 'My Dad Drank A Lot And Was Abusive'
item.description: Dave Mustaine, the founder of Megadeth and one of heavy metal’s most recognizable voices, has lived a life filled with music, fame, and success. But behind the guitars and sold-out shows is a past that’s far less glamorous.

item.title: Michael Paget Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's New Album Will Feature 'Crazy Tuning'
item.description: Guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is exploring new territory on their next studio album, including tunings the band has never used before. The longtime member of the Welsh metalcore group opened up about the upcoming record during a chat at this year’s Download Festival in the UK (watch the interview below).

item.title: KITTIE’s MORGAN LANDER Talks About Writing 'FIRE': 'It Was A Relearning Curve'
item.description: Getting back in the studio after more than a decade isn’t as simple as picking up where you left off. Just ask Morgan Lander. The guitarist and vocalist for Canadian metal band KITTIE says that writing Fire, their first album in 13 years, didn’t come with muscle memory (via TotalRock).

item.title: Creed's SCOTT STAPP On Viral Revival: 'It Started Online Before We Even Noticed'
item.description: Scott Stapp says the Creed reunion didn’t start with a grand plan or a flashy PR campaign. It began with the internet doing its thing. In a recent interview (via Meltdown), the singer explained that the band started to see signs of renewed interest around 2020, when clips, memes, and jokes about Creed started to go viral.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Reveals How the 'Terrible' LARS ULRICH Convinced Him to Start METALLICA
item.description: James Hetfield remembers the first time he met Lars Ulrich. According to him, Lars wasn’t exactly a great drummer when they crossed paths. Still, something about his energy made a lasting impression.

item.title: The Backstage Incident That Made KERRY KING Call a Rock Icon a 'Complete Jerk'
item.description: Not everyone in the world of music gets along, and that includes some of its biggest stars. Even in heavy metal, a genre known for its intensity and larger-than-life personalities, there are musicians who just don’t click.

item.title: AMY LEE Says New EVANESCENCE Album Coming 'Probably Early Next Year'
item.description: Evanescence is working on their next studio album, and according to Amy Lee, it’s likely to arrive in early 2026. The singer gave an update during a recent interview with WDHA-FM 105.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Breaks Silence on CHESTER BENNINGTON’s Death: 'Is It Even Called LINKIN PARK Anymore?'
item.description: Linkin Park bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell opened up about the band’s long road back to music after the loss of lead singer Chester Bennington. In a new interview with Czech station Evropa 2 (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: SCOTT STAPP Says CREED Is Rebuilding: 'We're Talking About New Music'
item.description: CREED frontman Scott Stapp says the band is easing back into things after more than a decade apart. In a recent interview, he shared that the group has been spending time together, reflecting on the past, and having early conversations about making new music (via Meltdown) (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Morgan Lander Says KITTIE May Release More Music: 'We’re Enjoying Ourselves'
item.description: KITTIE could be back in the studio again soon. Guitarist and vocalist Morgan Lander says the band is open to releasing more new music, thanks to the positive energy surrounding their recent reunion (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's Michael Paget On New Album: 'It's Gonna Be Super Heavy'
item.description: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is working on new music, and according to guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget, fans should expect something heavier than ever before. The Welsh metal band recently cut its joint tour with Trivium short, choosing to focus instead on writing and recording their next studio album.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The One Thing That Could End MEGADETH, According to DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Megadeth has been going strong for four decades, led from day one by guitarist, vocalist, and founding member Dave Mustaine. He’s the only constant in the thrash metal band’s long history and the driving force behind many of its best-known songs, including “Peace Sells,” “In My Darkest Hour,” “Holy Wars… The Punishment Due,” “Symphony of Destruction,” “A Tout Le Monde,” and “Trust.

item.title: MEGADETH's DAVE MUSTAINE On the 'Puppy Incident': 'JAMES Got Punched In The Mouth. He Kicked My Dog'
item.description: There’s no elegant way to introduce a story that ends with James Hetfield catching a mouthful of knuckles. Especially when the instigating factor was a puppy. But here we are.

item.title: Sodom's TOM ANGELRIPPER On Modern Metal Production: 'It's Cheap And It Shows'
item.description: Tom Angelripper has no patience for how modern metal is made. From his perspective, today’s studio habits cut corners and it’s obvious. “Recording in a digital way is cheap,” he said (via Blabbermouth).

item.title: Ex-EXODUS RICK HUNOLT Looks Back On Thrash Origins: 'We Inspired METALLICA And SLAYER'
item.description: Ex-EXODUS guitarist Rick Hunolt didn’t bother dancing around it during a recent chat with Pod Scum host Rexx Ruger (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.NET). When Ruger put Hunolt and Gary Holt on the same tier as Hetfield/Hammett or Hanneman/King, Hunolt didn’t blink.

item.title: CHARLIE BENANTE Says BLACK SABBATH Helped Shape ANTHRAX’s Sound: 'We Covered Sabbath Bloody Sabbath'
item.description: Anthrax drummer Charlie Benante pointed to Black Sabbath as a key influence on the band’s formative sound, recalling how their admiration for the Birmingham pioneers led them to cover Sabbath Bloody Sabbath during a formative period in their career.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.title: EUGENE ABDUKHANOV On MESHUGGAH's Early Days: 'People Didn’t Get It Then'
item.description: Eugene Abdukhanov isn’t new to giving credit where it’s due, even if it takes the rest of the world a couple of decades to catch up. Sitting down with Forever Loud at Download Festival, the JINJER bassist pulled no punches while looking back on what it was like watching MESHUGGAH rise from being the metal kid no one invited to the party, to becoming the very sound system (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Why Limp Bizkit’s FRED DURST Always Wore That RED BASEBALL CAP
item.description: Back in the early 2000s, nu metal was dominating the rock scene, with bands like Slipknot, Korn, Kid Rock, and Linkin Park in constant rotation on MTV.

item.title: The Heavy METALLICA Song That Tells the Story of JAMES HETFIELD’s Childhood TRAUMA
item.description: James Hetfield, guitarist and frontman of Metallica, didn’t exactly grow up riding rainbows. His early years were marked by the rigid dogma of a household that followed Christian Science, a belief system founded by Lafayette Ronald Hubbard (yep, the same guy behind Scientology).

item.title: STEVE DIGIORGIO On Recording With DAVE MUSTAINE: 'He Wasn't What I Expected'
item.description: Steve DiGiorgio, longtime bassist for Testament, has spoken candidly about his brief but intense experience recording with Dave Mustaine for Megadeth’s album The Sick, The Dying… And The Dead!

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On the 'Weak' METALLICA Member: 'Not Amazing'
item.description: James Hetfield has always been particular when it comes to Metallica’s music. Known for his precision as a rhythm guitarist, he’s often regarded as the most technically sharp member of the band, along with current bassist Robert Trujillo.

item.title: Ex-Pantera TERRY GLAZE On DIMEBAG's Death: 'It Didn't Hit Me Until I Saw The Dirt'
item.description: Former Pantera vocalist Terry Glaze has shared a personal account of how he learned about the death of guitarist “Dimebag” Darrell Abbott and the emotional aftermath that followed.

item.title: PAUL STANLEY On KISS Reunion Regrets: 'Some Nights Were Awful'
item.description: Turns out the face paint couldn’t cover everything. Back in 2000, KISS slapped the word farewell on a tour, grabbed the original lineup, and hit the road like it was 1977 all over again.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. SHADOWS On Being Misunderstood: 'People Are Just Getting It Now'
item.description: M. Shadows isn’t mad. He’s just… already moved on. If Life Is But a Dream… finally makes sense to you in 2025, congrats on solving the puzzle.

item.title: KORN Praises SLEEP TOKEN's Download Festival Show: 'They Outdid a SLIPKNOT Stage'
item.description: The members of Korn had high praise for Sleep Token following their performance at the Download Festival on Saturday, June 14. According to the band, the masked group managed to silence skeptics with a massive stage setup and commanding live presence.

item.title: The Day KORN Knocked a Guy Out Mid-Show… and Then WROTE A SONG About It
item.description: Not every song is born in a studio with clean instruments and sober minds. Some, like Korn’s Clown, crawl out of drug-fueled all-nighters in dingy apartments, shaped as much by the chaos around them as by the riffs themselves.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Talks About IRON MAIDEN Drama: 'It’s Just The Singer I Can’t Stand'
item.description: Sharon Osbourne still hasn’t let it go. Two decades after the absolute circus that was Ozzfest 2005, she’s perfectly willing to laugh about sabotaging Iron Maiden with beans, pre-recorded sound effects, and strategic sound cuts.

item.title: RINGO STARR Slams ROGER DALTREY Over Firing Of Son: 'Never Liked How That Little Man Runs The Band'
item.description: Zak Starkey didn’t bother hiding his disappointment after being pushed out of The Who, a gig he held for nearly 30 years as the band’s live drummer. It all unraveled after a messy show at the Royal Albert Hall earlier this year, which ultimately triggered the official announcement of his departure in April.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Says Younger Fans Ignore METALLICA Classics: 'They're More Into the New Stuff'
item.description: Not every Metallica fan has Master of Puppets tattooed on their brain. According to Lars Ulrich, a surprising number of listeners are skipping the band’s old-school thrash masterpieces in favor of more recent material.

item.title: JESSE LEACH Talks About KILLSWITCH ENGAGE's 'Aftermath': 'We All Have a Responsibility'
item.description: Killswitch Engage isn’t wasting time with metaphors or feel-good slogans in their latest single. The video for “Aftermath” just dropped, and it doesn’t sugarcoat a thing. If you were expecting a fun, breakdown-heavy anthem about “staying strong,” keep scrolling.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says MEGADETH Took Credit For 'Soldier On!': 'Just Wiped My Name Off'
item.description: David Ellefson isn’t done unpacking his past with Megadeth,and he’s brought receipts. In a new interview with The Delz Show, the former bassist draws some not-so-subtle contrasts between how Metallica handled songwriting credits with Dave Mustaine and how Mustaine allegedly did the opposite when it came to Megadeth’s own track, Soldier On!

item.title: BRIAN WELCH on KORN's New Album: 'We're Doing It All On Tape'
item.description: Korn is back in the studio, but don’t expect any instant gratification. This time, they’re ditching modern convenience for a much older, sweatier process. During a chat with BBC Radio 1’s Rock Show With Daniel P Carter (as transcribed by The PRP, guitarist Brian “Head” Welch explained that the band has fully embraced analog recording.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On His Father's Abandonment: 'He Didn't Even Say Goodbye'
item.description: Before the arenas, awards, and global tours, James Hetfield was just a kid growing up in the suburbs of Los Angeles. The setting looked ideal from the outside.

item.title: BLACK SABBATH's Tony Iommi Talks About Final Show Concerns: 'The Unknown Worries Me'
item.description: Tony Iommi, the ever-present architect of Black Sabbath, isn’t exactly sleeping easy as the band’s farewell inches closer. Set for July 5 in Birmingham, England, the hometown gig isn’t just another concert.

item.title: PIGGY D. On Working With MARILYN MANSON: 'I'm Proud To Stand Next To Him'
item.description: Matt Montgomery, better known as Piggy D., isn’t shy when it comes to describing his experience playing bass for Marilyn Manson. In a recent interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: IHSAHN Explains Why GHOST, SLEEP TOKEN And SLIPKNOT Attract Crowds: 'It's The Masks, The Visuals, The Mystery'
item.description: Ihsahn has no interest in blurring the lines between personal life and stage persona. In his opinion, keeping those worlds apart explains why bands like Ghost, Sleep Token, and Slipknot generate such obsessive fascination.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Recalls METALLICA Audition: 'My Mom Used To Clean Lars' Apartment'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t need to strike a single chord to sense the outcome of his audition for Metallica. After spotting their ad in a magazine, he reached out to Lars Ulrich and arranged to meet up in Newport Beach for a live tryout.

item.title: DUFF MCKAGAN Compares OZZY OSBOURNE to Lemmy, Prince, and Iggy Pop
item.description: Duff McKagan has seen plenty of rock stars come and go, but when it comes to Ozzy Osbourne, he doesn’t mince words. “A constant in rock and roll,” as he puts it.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Says FAITH NO MORE's Mike Patton Is 'An Unprofessional Jerk'
item.description: Dave Mustaine has spent over 40 years running the Megadeth machine as guitarist, vocalist, songwriter, and self-appointed keeper of thrash metal’s purity. In that time, he’s built not only an impressive discography, but a side hustle in speaking his mind with the grace of a sledgehammer.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On Metallica T-Shirts: 'I’m Not Sure I Want Them Wearing That'
item.description: Plenty of metalheads have their rituals. They blast albums, whether on vinyl, cassette, or whatever streaming service rules the moment. They pack venues when the tour bus rolls into town.

item.title: MATT TUCK Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE Will Return To Studio: 'We Can't Wait To Drop New Music'
item.description: While stomping around Donington Park for the Download Festival in the UK, Matt Tuck finally offered something resembling an update on Bullet For My Valentine’s elusive eighth studio album.

item.title: DAVID VINCENT Reflects On Fan Expectations: 'Nobody Cares About The New Stuff'
item.description: David Vincent, the former Morbid Angel frontman, isn’t exactly rushing to crank out new material with I Am Morbid. In a recent sit-down with Altars Of Metal, the inevitable question popped up: will I Am Morbid ever release original songs?

item.title: What James Hetfield And Robert Trujillo Would Do If Metallica Never Existed
item.description: Episode 98 of The Metallica Report tossed out a simple question that got James Hetfield and Robert Trujillo thinking about an alternate universe where Metallica never happened. The fan-submitted query from Denmark asked them to picture their lives without the band that has basically defined them.

item.title: David Ellefson: "I Miss Dave" But I’m Done With Megadeth’s Drama
item.description: David Ellefson still feels the absence of Dave Mustaine in his life, even after everything. In a recent chat with The Delz Show, Ellefson reflected: “I miss Dave too.

item.title: Kirk Hammett Rules Out Retirement From Metallica Despite 62 Years of Age
item.description: Kirk Hammett has no interest in slowing down. Speaking to Metal Hammer, he dismissed the idea of retirement entirely. “I don’t believe in retirement. Retirement is something that’s been forced onto people; I don’t believe musicians are allowed to retire,” he said.

item.title: Lzzy Hale Opens Up About New Vocal Mastery After 28 Years Fronting Halestorm
item.description: Long before Lzzy Hale stood under arena lights, she was perched in a dogwood tree somewhere along the Appalachian Trail, testing her voice against the leaves and scaring squirrels.

item.title: James Hetfield Shares The Cost of Fame: ‘They Think They Know Me’
item.description: Metallica’s new documentary, Metallica Saved My Life, made its debut at the Tribeca Festival in New York City on June 11. After the screening, all four band members joined The New Yorker’s Amanda Petrusich for a conversation that pulled back the curtain on both their private lives and the inspiration behind the film.

item.title: David Ellefson Breaks Down Megadeth’s Risk and Its Divisive Legacy
item.description: In 1999, Megadeth rolled the dice with Risk, a record that veered sharply away from the band’s thrash metal identity. For David Ellefson, the album remains, in his own words, “probably the most controversial album in the catalog.

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Dream Theater’s Mike Portnoy on Pain, Perseverance, and Playing Through Injury
item.description: Step into this scene with me… Dream Theater, mid-’90s, prog-metal gods playing Awake on tour—Portnoy’s behind the kit, hair flailing, sticks a blur, sweat dripping like he’s trying to personally refill the Dead Sea.

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: Clown Admits He Was a “Naysayer” About Revisiting Slipknot’s First Album
item.description: It’s 2025, and somehow Slipknot is still here, still wearing masks, still smashing percussion instruments like cavemen discovering fire, but also—shockingly—getting reflective about their past. Yes, you read that right: Shawn “Clown” Crahan, the band’s resident chaos conductor, actually sat down and got nostalgic.

item.title: Lorraine Lewis on Joining OnlyFans: "It’s Sexy, I’m Owning It, And I’m Having Fun!"
item.description: Lorraine Lewis. 66 years old. Rock icon. Ex-VIXEN. Current FEMME FATALE badass. Also? Now officially on OnlyFans. And not just dipping her toes in—she’s fully in the pool.

item.title: Heidi Shepherd Speaks Out on Vocal Training: “I Was a Singer Before I Was a Screamer”
item.description: Apparently some people still think Heidi Shepherd—frontwoman of BUTCHER BABIES, growler of unholy things, destroyer of vocal cords (except, not hers, more on that later)—can’t sing. And she’s had enough.

item.title: Grammy Interviewer Mistakes Spiritbox’s Courtney LaPlante for Poppy—See the Full Video
item.description: Yeah babe, the Grammys. A night of glitz, glamour, and—if we’re being honest—rock and metal getting shoved to the side like an unwanted side dish at a fancy dinner.

item.title: Max Cavalera on Re-Recording SEPULTURA’s Early Albums: “They Never Sounded Right”
item.description: Oh boy, here we go. Another “let’s redo our old stuff, but this time better” kind of deal. You know, like when you rewrite a high school essay as an adult and suddenly realize, wow, I really didn’t understand metaphors back then.

item.title: Sharon den Adel Confirms Within Temptation’s Next Album Is Taking Shape: “We Have a Clear Vision”
item.description: So Within Temptation has a plan. Well, sort of. Sharon den Adel insists they “really have an idea what we wanna do next,” which sounds promising—until you realize that the band started with the intention of taking their sweet time, only to immediately flip-flop.

item.title: Bush’s Gavin Rossdale on the Music Industry: “I Can’t Work Out How Young Bands Get Paid”
item.description: Gavin Rossdale, frontman of Bush, seems genuinely lost when it comes to figuring out how young bands actually make money these days, and honestly? Same. The guy flat-out said, “I can’t work it out,” and if that isn’t the most relatable statement about the modern music industry, I don’t know what is.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. Shadows Talks God, Purpose, and Fear
item.description: Deep in conversation on the “Artist Friendly With Joel Madden” podcast, the 43-year-old frontman for AVENGED SEVENFOLD, M. Shadows (real name: Matt Sanders), pulled no punches on religion and spirituality.

item.title: Michael Wilton Talks New Queensrÿche Album and 2025 Goals
item.description: Queensrÿche guitarist Michael Wilton spoke with Robert Cavuoto (for MyGlobalMind). Touched on new record plans? Absolutely. Also reflected on the many twists and turns the band has faced over the decades (and there have been plenty).

item.title: Necrobutcher on Mayhem's Four Decades of Survival
item.description: When the bassist of your band murders the guitarist, you’d think the group might call it quits. Most bands implode over petty squabbles about songwriting credits or tour schedules—not criminal trials.

item.title: L7’s Donita Sparks on the Band’s Unique Place in Rock: ‘We’re an Outlier’
item.description: Donita Sparks from L7—a band often shoved into the ‘90s grunge box but sounding more like MOTÖRHEAD after too much coffee—sat down with Australia’s Heavy. And the question came up: how would she describe their sound?

item.title: John Corabi on Mötley Crüe Exit: "Relieved and Bummed"
item.description: John Corabi (yes, the guy who briefly fronted Mötley Crüe) sat down for an interview and spilled—well, not tea exactly, but maybe lukewarm coffee. His time with the band?

item.title: Ryan McCombs Wishes Social Media Never Existed—But He Still Uses It
item.description: Ryan McCombs—frontman of Drowning Pool and SOIL, master of growls, occasional philosopher—has thoughts about social media. Big ones. Messy ones. The kind that make you nod along until he throws in a time-travel fantasy about stopping Zuckerberg in his tracks (we’ll get there).

item.title: Why Tommy Lee Showers Once a Week, According to His Wife
item.description: Tommy Lee, drummer for Mötley Crüe, bathes sparingly. His wife, Brittany Furlan, says he showers only once a week. The detail emerged on Kaitlyn Bristowe’s Off the Vine podcast, where Furlan spoke about her husband’s habits.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda: “Our New Lineup Came Together Naturally”
item.description: Linkin Park is back. New album (listen below). New lineup. Same vibe. This one’s called “From Zero”, which feels like a bit of an oversell for a band that’s been rehashing itself since 2017.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: SKILLET's John Cooper on Political Divides in Rock: "We're Shut Out"
item.description: In a recent chat with the Rebellious Remarks podcast, John Cooper, frontman for SKILLET, took the opportunity to drop some of his usual truth bombs about being a Christian rock musician in today’s ultra-polarized world.

item.title: Ted Nugent Praises Metallica’s "Soulful" Groove While Criticizing Pantera
item.description: In a recent episode of Ted Nugent’s show “Spirit Campfire” on Real America’s Voice, the ever-outspoken Nugent threw a nod to several rockers who are still out there tearing up stages, mentioning Mark Farner, STYX, and Sammy Hagar as some of the enduring performers.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: Clown on New Slipknot Music: “Delivered in a Way You Can’t Imagine”
item.description: Slipknot has been on a tear lately. Between nostalgia-drenched 25th-anniversary shows and an endless parade of collaborations (because why not?), the band’s summer could be described as anything but boring.

item.title: Metallica's Kirk Hammett Declares Judas Priest the True Founders of Heavy Metal
item.description: Kirk Hammett isn’t here to play revisionist history with metal. When the drummer Carmine Appice tossed out the claim that heavy metal only began with Metallica, some folks had a field day.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Jim Root: “Slipknot Is Lucky to Have Eloy Casagrande”
item.description: Slipknot’s Jim Root isn’t holding back his admiration for the band’s newest drumming powerhouse, Eloy Casagrande. If Root’s comments are anything to go by, it seems the band practically stumbled into the perfect fit without breaking a sweat—or even auditioning anyone else.

item.title: Linkin Park Rumored to Return with a Female Lead Singer
item.description: July marks seven years since Chester Bennington’s untimely passing—a moment that shattered not just his family and friends, but the entire world of Linkin Park fans. His death wasn’t just tragic; it was a full stop.

item.title: Korn’s Creative Process: Ray Luzier Breaks Down the Band’s Approach
item.description: Korn’s drummer, Ray Luzier, has been pounding the skins for the band since 2007, and he’s got plenty of stories to tell. In a chat with Modern Drummer, Luzier reflected on some of the band’s most memorable moments, from their biggest hits to their more out-there experiments.

item.title: Amy Lee Reflects on Bring Me to Life's Rap: "Not My Style"
item.description: Amy Lee, the unmistakable voice of Evanescence, hasn’t minced words about her feelings toward the now-iconic rap segment in Bring Me to Life. For two decades, she’s openly expressed her discomfort with the label-driven decision to shoehorn in Paul McCoy’s rap—something neither she nor the band originally envisioned for their breakout hit.
